newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha falls but hinges on Med cargoes, swaps.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha falls but hinges on Med cargoes, swaps.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices fell modestly after a selloff in crude, but traders warned that the next big move hinged on the swaps market and at least three large Med cargoes looking for homes.

Heavy swaps buying again was visible on Monday, with four noted buyers and one seller, to underscore strength in the paper market and widen the Feb/March spread, to an $8 backwardation from $6 on Friday, traders said.
Feb swaps lost $3 to $225/$226 a tonne while March dropped $5 to $217/$218. April fell $6 to $211/$212.

"It's very well supported," in the swaps, said one London trader. "It all depends on where the cargoes end up. If they end up in Northwest Europe, I can't believe a $3 (a barrel) crack spread is justified."

He said the crack spread between Feb naphtha swaps and the front-month Brent crude jumped from about $1.75 a barrel to $3 in the last 10 sessions -- punctuating what some traders in the market are calling a potential squeeze.

The three cargoes that will tip the balance are between 50,000 and 60,000 tonnes of north African material, traders said. Rumours have circulated as to whether they will end up in Northwest Europe, Spain, the U.S. or Brazil.

One trader said there were rumours one of them, a 50,000 tonne Skikda cargo, was being offered into Northwest Europe, even though the vessel only has options for the U.S. or South America, in order to knock down NWE prices.
Another cargo may be headed to Tarragona, Spain, while the third is still uncertain, he said.
"I don't see that it makes sense to go to the States," he said, predicting NWE prices would fall sharply if the cargoes end up here.
End-user demand is generally quiet as the NWE market is "quite balanced to maybe a bit long," he said. Some fob barrels for the ARA region were also on offer, he said.
NWE cargoes were assessed at even to slightly above the swaps prices, at about $224/$228 cif, he said.
Med cargoes were notionally valued $3 below that with fob barrels still holding a wide discount of about $16 due to the high freight rates that have hampered buying.
